prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: parking lot collision in Sugar Land, Texas. Injury: concussion. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1074; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not use my full name on the record, if that's okay. You can call me the plaintiff.
Q: Understood. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in a parking lot in Sugar Land, Texas, at a shopping center. I had just pulled into a spot near the entrance.
Q: Which direction were you traveling when you entered the space?
A: I was driving slowly, maybe five miles an hour, looking for an open spot. The other vehicle was backing out of a space two rows over.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before the impact?
A: Not really. I saw a flash of white out of the corner of my window, and then there was a hard jolt. My head hit the side window and the airbag went off.
Q: Did you lose consciousness at any point?
A: I don't think I fully blacked out, but everything went fuzzy for a few seconds. I remember sitting there trying to figure out where I was.
Q: When did you first notice symptoms?
A: Within an hour or so I had a splitting headache, and the lights in the store were painful to look at. By that evening I was nauseous and felt confused when I tried to read my messages.
Q: Did you seek medical care?
A: Yes, I went to the emergency room that same day. They did a CT scan and told me I had a concussion. They gave me instructions to rest and avoid screens as much as possible.
Q: Have you followed up with any other providers?
A: I've seen my primary care doctor a few times, and I was referred to a neurologist. I also did some vision therapy because my eyes had trouble tracking movement for weeks.
Q: How has the injury affected your daily life?
A: Pretty significantly. I had to step back from work for a while because I couldn't stay focused on a computer for more than a few minutes. Reading is still harder than it used to be, and I get headaches if I'm in a loud room.
Q: Have you been able to do your usual activities at home?
A: Not fully. I used to cook and go running several times a week. Now I'm limited to short walks, and my family has had to help with a lot of the household tasks.
Q: Do you still have symptoms today?
A: Some of them, yes. The headaches have gotten less frequent, but I still have occasional dizziness and trouble sleeping through the night.
